best_for: Remote teams on Windows or Mac who explain work with short screen recordings instead of meetings, and who will pay per seat once five-minute clips feel tight.

points.title: Free stops at five minutes
points.text: The free Starter plan caps screen recordings at 5 minutes and each person at 25 videos, with playback up to 720p. It works for quick replies and bug reports, not for walkthroughs or training.

points.title: Business is the paid line
points.text: Business is listed at USD 18 per user per month and removes the video and length limits, adds 4K, uploads and downloads, password-protected videos and removal of Loom branding. Business + AI is USD 24 and adds auto titles, summaries, chapters and filler-word removal. Yearly billing saves up to 17%. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Trials and admin controls
points.text: Business + AI has a 14-day free trial; SSO and SCIM sit in the Enterprise plan, which has no public price.

points.title: Newest Mac app wants macOS 15
points.text: Loom's compatibility page says the newest Mac app needs macOS 15, and an older app remains for macOS 12.3 and later. Both need an Apple silicon Mac or an Intel Mac from 2018 onward, 8 GB of RAM and 16 GB free on the system drive.

points.title: Windows needs a 6th-gen Intel or better
points.text: On Windows, Loom asks for Windows 10 or later, an Intel 6th Gen (Skylake) or comparable AMD processor and 8 GB of RAM, with 16 GB recommended. The app may open on older machines, but recording can fail. The installer sets up the app for the current user only.

points.title: No Linux app
points.text: Loom makes desktop apps for Windows and Mac only. Linux and ChromeOS are not supported as desktop platforms.

points.title: Older versions on Windows only
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 207 versions. macOS lists only the current release, so going back on a Mac needs another source.
